subject.title: Feature Request: Plugin Circuit Breaker for graceful degradation

question: Should OpenClaw add a framework-level plugin hook/tool circuit breaker, and what storage, fail-mode, status/reset, and default-on contract should it expose?
rationale: The missing capability is real in source, but choosing active fail behavior, forced-open state, operator controls, and plugin API surface changes runtime compatibility and third-party plugin expectations.

options.title: Design Core Breaker Contract First
options.body: Define the generic hook/tool breaker API, SQLite state schema, status/reset surfaces, passive telemetry rollout, and upgrade-safe default before implementation.

options.title: Keep Breakers Plugin-Owned
options.body: Continue plugin-local breakers like Active Memory and add only narrow SDK helpers when repeated plugin needs prove a shared contract.

options.title: Start With Log-Only Telemetry
options.body: Add attribution and passive breaker evaluation first, then decide active open/half-open behavior after real deployment data.

recommendation.title: Design Core Breaker Contract First
recommendation.body: Define the generic hook/tool breaker API, SQLite state schema, status/reset surfaces, passive telemetry rollout, and upgrade-safe default before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: Current blame and recent history place Vincent Koc on the exact hook, tool, session-lock, runtime-health, and Active Memory surfaces that would carry the design.
